name: altar

attributes.attribute: stone altars are a Roman custom
was a rough boulder or rock heap

sources: MacCulloch, J. A. The Religion of the Ancient Celts. London: Constable, 1911, 283.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: An altar is a Celtic ritual object. Stone altars cut with tributes to Celtic gods have been found in Britain and on the Continent. They show Roman custom, not Celtic practice. Several writers speak of altars the Celts used for offering. The Roman author Cicero and the Irish Cormac both do. Those altars were not the carved tables the legions brought to Celtic lands. The Celts worshiped outdoors. So their first altars were likely rough boulders or heaps of big stone. See Sacrifice.
